dcos.ci_note: doc-level: per-doc median, bootstrap over 32 docs
dcos.mean_note: flat mean over N*S positions — NOT comparable to the median (median-of-per-doc-medians): different aggregates (docs/E38_fixes.md §38f)
dcos.g_not_top_note: fraction of (doc,t) where argmax_k |c_k| picked a non-top mode: excluded from the verdict (NaN), Δcos >= 0 does not follow for k != 0 (docs/E38_fixes.md §38f P0)
dcos.frac_above_note: per-position Δcos > 1 - c_g + eps (c_g per position): sensitivity diagnostic, not a verdict (per-doc median hides a single anomalous position), docs/E38_fixes.md §38f

meta.note: |cos| used (sign(v_g) non-unique, LAPACK); c_k = (U.T @ one)[k] = |u_k·1/√K| (the old (U @ one)[k] row-metric was a bug, part-7 §1); the lemma J^T u = c β v_⊥ is an exact identity — the cos test measures the EMPIRICAL alignment v_⊥ ∥ v_g. The Δcos ≥ 0 range is a consequence of the lemma ONLY for g = top mode: (doc, t) with argmax c_k at k != 0 are EXCLUDED from the verdict (NaN) and counted in g_not_top_frac — a non-top pick can give Δcos << 0 without violating the lemma (P0, docs/E38_fixes.md §38f; supersedes docs/E38_fixes2.md). Δcos < −eps = empirical_alignment_violated, ≤ 1−c_g+eps = empirical_alignment_within_range, above = methodological_anomaly. eps = 0.05 is a STATISTICAL tolerance, not a numerical one (float32 SVD noise is ~1e-7; 0.05 = 1e5× that): a 'within_range' verdict on Δcos ∈ [−eps, 0) is empirical, not lemma-exact. dcos median is a NaN-excluding median (nanmedian); nan_count/nan_frac record the degenerate ‖J^T u‖ ≈ 0 subset; vpred_degenerate_frac the v_pred_from_JT RuntimeErrors
meta.labels_renamed: verdict labels renamed from the pre-registered lemma_confirmed / lemma_broken to empirical_alignment_within_range / empirical_alignment_violated: the lemma is an exact identity, the test measures empirical alignment (docs/E38_fixes.md §38f)
